title: Mechanism-based prevention of chronic postsurgical pain

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a way to identify and safely interrupt biological processes that turn surgical injury into persistent pain. An intervention given around surgery would target a causally important transition process in a defined patient or procedure group, with the aim of preventing lasting pain and disability. The breakthrough would combine an explanation of why persistent pain develops with a practical way to change that outcome.

Conceptual scope: the research starts from the working premise that persistent postsurgical pain can have multiple contributing mechanisms, potentially differing among patients and operations. The supplied accessible evidence does not establish that premise or identify particular mechanisms. The concept therefore allows several targeted prevention strategies rather than requiring one universal treatment. Its defining outcome is durable prevention; immediate pain relief alone would not demonstrate success.

significance.text: Conditional significance: reliable prevention would allow perioperative care to avert a lasting consequence of surgery rather than address it only after it develops. If the effect were substantial and extended across major procedures, it could change the long-term outcomes patients can expect from surgery. A strategy effective only in a narrower, well-defined group could still be valuable, but would support a correspondingly narrower claim.

Conditional downstream possibilities include better long-term function and less need for continuing pain treatment. These outcomes would require measurement rather than inference from a reduction in pain incidence. In particular, lower chronic-pain incidence would not automatically establish lower long-term opioid use. The scale of benefit would depend on the patients reached, the durability and magnitude of the effect, and whether prevention preserves healing without unacceptable adverse effects.

Conceptual limit: suppressing pain during or immediately after surgery does not by itself show that the transition to persistent pain has been interrupted. Nor would successful prevention prove that every case shares one biological cause. The revolutionary capability would be demonstrated causal prevention within an established scope, with broader applicability remaining a separate question.

missing_breakthrough.text: Proposed research gap: an actionable, causally supported method is needed to determine which transition processes should be interrupted, in whom, and when. Identifying a feature associated with later pain would be insufficient by itself; the strategy must establish that changing the targeted process changes persistent-pain outcomes. The supplied evidence does not establish how much of this capability already exists, so the gap should not be read as a verified claim that no actionable causal approaches are available.

Scientific and engineering barriers, inferred from the proposed goal, include distinguishing causal processes from accompanying signs of injury, selecting patients or procedures likely to benefit, and delivering an intervention during an effective perioperative window. If different groups require different targets, the practical advance would also need a usable way to select the appropriate strategy. A benefit observed in one operation cannot simply be assumed to transfer to another.

A further proposed barrier is achieving durable prevention while preserving recovery. Target engagement and short-term analgesia would need to be connected to later patient-important outcomes, with healing and adverse effects assessed directly. An intervention that changes early pain but leaves persistent pain and disability unchanged would not satisfy the central goal.

current_state.text: The supplied research reports a systematic review and network meta-analysis by Martin Taylor-Rowan and colleagues, titled “Regional anaesthesia and chronic postsurgical pain: a systematic review and network meta-analysis,” attributed to the British Journal of Anaesthesia, online 9 July 2026, DOI 10.1016/j.bja.2026.04.082. It reports 158 randomized trials, lower chronic postsurgical pain incidence with regional anesthesia versus no block, low-certainty evidence for the chronic-pain finding, and no statistically significant reduction in long-term opioid use. These are reported findings from the research input; the supplied review could not independently verify the article identity, date, trial count, comparisons, certainty rating, or outcomes.

The evidence limitation is specific: the retained response at the supplied PubMed URL contained only a cookie interstitial, without an article title, authors, abstract, or scientific discussion. Although the source index records a saved artifact, that artifact does not substantiate the attributed findings. The research states that full text was not inspected. This access limitation leaves the claims unverified in the supplied materials; it is not evidence that the reported review or results are false.

Conditional interpretation of the reported result: if accurately described, a reduction in chronic-pain incidence would support partial prevention in the studied settings. It would not establish complete prevention, one universal causal mechanism, or reliable benefit across all major procedures. Low-certainty evidence would limit confidence in the effect, and a statistically nonsignificant opioid result would establish neither a reduction nor the absence of any possible effect. The supplied materials do not provide effect sizes, follow-up intervals, procedure-specific results, or sufficient comparator detail to define the clinical magnitude and boundaries.

Evidence-scope limitation: the supplied record does not verify an achieved mechanism-based prevention capability or establish comprehensively how far the field remains from it. No bounded search entries were supplied. The source retrieval timestamp of 11 November 2026 establishes when a response was saved, not that the literature was covered through 1 November 2026 or any other cutoff.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration, not an established consensus standard: mechanistic studies would identify an intervention target and provide causal evidence connecting its modification to prevention of persistent pain. The intended patient or procedure groups would be specified in advance, along with an operational method for selecting them and delivering the intervention.
completion_criteria.label: Target modification causally prevents persistent pain in prespecified groups

completion_criteria.text: Independently replicated randomized trials would then show a substantial, durable reduction in clinically meaningful persistent pain and pain-related disability compared with good contemporary care. Before testing, investigators would define what counts as substantial benefit, the follow-up duration needed to assess persistence and durability, and the care included in the comparator. Those definitions would need clinical justification; the supplied record does not provide established numerical thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Randomized trials independently replicate substantial, durable pain and disability reductions

completion_criteria.text: Trials would measure adverse effects and healing alongside benefit, and assess longer-term treatment use directly if reductions in that use are claimed. Independent replication would test reproducibility, while studies across additional operations and patient groups would establish the demonstrated breadth of prevention. Finite studies could justify use within tested boundaries and support carefully qualified generalization; they could not establish literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Trials report adverse effects, healing, and demonstrated prevention breadth

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: ANS-03, “A broadly applicable, pain-selective surgical nerve block,” concerns a blocking capability for surgery, while ANS-07, “Systemic, non-opioid analgesia for severe perioperative pain,” concerns systemic treatment of severe perioperative pain. Either could contribute to ANS-09 if trials demonstrated durable prevention of persistent pain. Their stated capabilities alone would not establish that outcome, and ANS-09 need not depend exclusively on either modality. Only their titles and the candidate's brief comparison were supplied, so detailed technical overlap remains unassessed.

Roster-based comparison: ANS-10, “Mechanism-guided anesthesia to prevent postoperative brain dysfunction,” shares the idea of using perioperative mechanisms to prevent a later adverse outcome. Its stated outcome is brain dysfunction, whereas ANS-09 concerns persistent pain and related disability. A shared prevention framework does not establish shared mechanisms, interventions, or evidence.

Roster-based comparison: ANS-01, “A causal theory of anesthetic-induced unconsciousness,” ANS-02, “A reliable real-time monitor of conscious experience during anesthesia,” ANS-04, “Surgical unconsciousness with preserved breathing and circulatory control,” and ANS-06, “Broad, active reversal of general anesthesia,” address understanding, monitoring, producing, or reversing anesthetic unconsciousness. They occupy the same perioperative setting but have different primary outcomes from prevention of persistent pain. The supplied roster establishes no necessary dependency between them and ANS-09.

Roster-based comparison: ANS-05, “A radically accessible, resilient anesthesia platform for essential surgery,” concerns access and delivery, while ANS-08, “Reliable rescue oxygenation in the difficult airway,” concerns airway rescue. A future ANS-09 intervention might need to fit practical anesthesia delivery systems, but neither platform access nor successful oxygenation would itself demonstrate chronic-pain prevention. These relationships are conceptual comparisons based on the supplied titles.

brief.title: Preventing lasting pain after surgery
possible: People having surgery could receive treatment that stops pain from becoming a lasting part of their lives. Care around the operation would target a biological process that causes pain to persist, with the treatment chosen for the patient or procedure.
why: Surgery could leave fewer people with lasting pain and disability. Prevention would become part of surgical care, rather than leaving patients to seek treatment once persistent pain develops.
Successful prevention could also help people regain everyday function and reduce their need for continuing pain treatment.

sources.showed: Their review found less lasting pain after regional anaesthesia, which numbs part of the body, than without a nerve block. Confidence in the pain finding was low. They found no statistically significant difference in long-term opioid painkiller use.
sources.quote: Our findings indicate that regional anaesthesia reduces the incidence of CPSP for up to 12 months after surgery.
sources.cited_for: Nerve blocks can reduce the chance of lasting pain after surgery.
sources.not_established: The review does not establish which biological process caused the benefit or demonstrate reliable prevention across operations.

sources.who: Sophie Laumet and colleagues at Michigan State University
sources.showed: In mice, blocking TNFα, an immune signal involved in inflammation, prolonged sensitivity to pain after a surgical cut. The effect occurred in both sexes.
sources.quote: Unexpectedly, early blockade of TNFα signaling did not reduce pain hypersensitivity but instead extended its duration.
sources.cited_for: An immune signal associated with inflammation can also help pain resolve after surgery.
sources.not_established: This mouse study does not demonstrate a treatment that safely prevents lasting pain in people.

sources.who: Sarah Baos and the GAP Investigators
sources.showed: Their randomized trial compared gabapentin, a pain medicine, with a placebo after major surgery. More participants given gabapentin reported pain after leaving hospital.
sources.cited_for: Giving a pain medicine around surgery does not necessarily prevent later pain.
sources.not_established: The trial does not demonstrate prevention by changing a biological process that causes pain to persist.

shown: Martin Taylor-Rowan and colleagues found that nerve blocks reduced lasting pain after surgery, with effects seen up to 12 months. Confidence in the finding was low. This supports partial prevention, but does not establish why it works.

Sophie Laumet and colleagues showed in mice that blocking an inflammatory immune signal delayed pain recovery. That identifies a process involved in recovery, but does not yet provide a preventive treatment for people.
missing: A treatment must change a biological cause of persistent pain, with a practical way to select who receives it and when.
Independent trials must demonstrate lasting reductions in meaningful pain and disability compared with good current care.
Prevention must preserve healing, have acceptable adverse effects and establish which patients and operations benefit.

milestones.label: Changing a biological target prevents persistent pain in defined groups
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to show that changing a biological target prevents persistent pain in patient or procedure groups chosen in advance. This would establish a causal basis for choosing and timing treatment.

milestones.label: Independent trials confirm lasting reductions in pain and disability
milestones.explanation: Independent randomized trials would have to confirm substantial, lasting reductions in pain and disability against good current care. Clinically justified definitions would make the benefit meaningful and reproducible.

milestones.label: Trials establish harms, healing and the breadth of prevention
milestones.explanation: Trials would have to measure harms, healing and any claimed reduction in treatment use, with independent replication across further operations and patient groups. This would establish safe use and the reach of prevention.

uncertain: Do different patients and operations require different biological targets?
How large and lasting must the benefit be, and what harms would be acceptable?
Would preventing persistent pain also reduce long-term opioid use?

page.title: Mechanism-based prevention of chronic postsurgical pain
page.definition: A treatment given around the time of a specified operation would reduce the risk of persistent pain by changing a biological process that causes it. Chronic postsurgical pain begins or worsens after surgery and persists beyond expected healing for at least three months after the operation. It is felt in the operated area, in the territory of a nerve there, or in an area to which pain from the operated tissues is referred. Diagnosis requires excluding other causes, including infection, malignancy and continuation of pre-existing pain.

goal.need: About 1 in 10 surgical patients develops persistent pain and about 1 in 100 develops severe persistent pain. Greater pain severity is associated with more difficulty in daily activities six and twelve months later. Better pain relief in hospital can leave that risk intact. After major surgery, adding gabapentin slightly reduced pain on the first day, yet more patients reported pain four months later. Preventing the transition could spare patients months of pain and disability if the treatment addresses a cause of persistent pain for their operation.

completion.title: Independent trials replicate mechanism-based prevention of chronic postsurgical pain at twelve months.
completion.criterion: In a defined surgical population, a perioperative intervention achieves its prespecified clinically important reduction in chronic postsurgical pain at 12 months in a randomized controlled trial, with independent randomized replication. Human experimental evidence establishes that modifying the proposed biological target changes the preventive effect. The trials demonstrate their prespecified functional benefit and meet protocol-defined healing and safety criteria. Numerical benefit and harm thresholds come from the registered protocols and their clinical justification.
completion.set_by: Atlas. No external body defines this combined test of causal mechanism, twelve-month clinical benefit, safety and independent replication.
completion.basis: IMMPACT recommends assessing postsurgical pain at 3, 6 and 12 months when feasible. The Federal Pain Research Strategy working group calls for mechanistic prevention trials that assess functional recovery. The Atlas selects the twelve-month endpoint and requires independent randomized replication, human evidence that the target contributes causally to prevention, and protocol-defined functional, healing and safety outcomes.

milestones.title: A postsurgical pain target is validated across animal models, laboratories or human tissue.
milestones.criterion: Validate a target relevant to postsurgical pain in multiple animal models, by reproducing the finding in another laboratory, or by experimental validation in human tissue.
milestones.set_by: NIH HEAL Initiative, RFA-NS-22-034, Research Objectives. Its published criterion covers pain targets generally, including postoperative pain.
milestones.threshold_quote: rigorously validating the target using multiple animal models, reproducing the work in another laboratory, or in human tissue etc.

milestones.title: A perioperative intervention engages its proposed biological target in surgical patients.
milestones.criterion: In a controlled study of surgical patients, a perioperative dose that meets the protocol's safety criteria produces the intended change in an objective measure of the proposed biological target.
milestones.set_by: Atlas. Searches of NIH pain programmes, IMMPACT recommendations and postsurgical prevention protocols found no shared human target-engagement success threshold. The Federal Pain Research Strategy working group calls for evaluating mechanisms discovered in animals in humans.

milestones.title: A randomized trial shows lower chronic postsurgical pain incidence at three months.
milestones.criterion: A randomized superiority trial finds a lower incidence of adjudicated chronic postsurgical pain at three months with the perioperative intervention than with control. The confidence interval corresponding to the prespecified test lies wholly on the side of benefit: below 1 for an intervention-to-control risk ratio or below 0 for an intervention-minus-control risk difference. For an individual operation, apply the test to an estimate for that operation. ROCKet specifies a 95.1% interval for its pooled ketamine comparison.
milestones.set_by: Committee for Proprietary Medicinal Products, guidance on superiority trials. IMMPACT recommends three-month assessment when feasible. Each protocol specifies its analysis and confidence level.
milestones.threshold_quote: it is the position of the confidence interval for the test statistic relative to this ‘no difference’ value that is of interest.

milestones.title: One mechanistic trial reduces chronic postsurgical pain and pain-related disability at twelve months.
milestones.criterion: In one randomized trial in a specified surgical population, the intervention achieves the prespecified reductions in chronic postsurgical pain and pain-related disability at twelve months. The trial verifies target engagement, demonstrates that changing the target contributes causally to prevention, and meets the protocol's healing and safety criteria.
milestones.set_by: Atlas. IMMPACT recommends 12-month assessment and ROCKet registers a 12-month endpoint. Searches found no common composite success test covering human mechanism, prevention, function and safety. This stage requires one qualifying trial before independent replication.

milestones.title: Changing a biological target alters the duration of hypersensitivity in a surgical animal model.
milestones.criterion: In a controlled animal experiment, manipulate a specified target around surgery and follow a pain-related response over time. The treated and control groups differ in how long postoperative hypersensitivity persists. Either faster or slower resolution can identify a target's role.
milestones.set_by: Atlas. No outside body defines a common single-model test for a target's role in postsurgical pain resolution.

not_found: Searches yielded no field-wide numerical thresholds for human target engagement, preventive benefit, functional benefit or acceptable healing and adverse-event differences.
Searches of ANZCTR, ANZCA and PubMed found no main ROCKet efficacy report.
The accessible regional-anaesthesia abstract supplies no operation-specific twelve-month estimates or subgroup sample sizes.
Searches of pain-society statements, regulatory guidance and research priorities found no institutional objection to pursuing prevention of chronic postsurgical pain.

Searches of postsurgical prevention trials found no independently replicated twelve-month result combining causal target evidence, pain and functional benefit, and prespecified healing and safety outcomes.

results.finding: After total knee arthroplasty, three-month neuropathic pain incidence was 8.7 percentage points lower with pregabalin (228 assessed).

results.detail: The 12-month intention-to-treat pain comparison is reported in Table 3. WOMAC knee scores covered pain, stiffness, and daily function.

results.finding: Total knee arthroplasty (69 completers). The ketamine–placebo difference in 12-month pain prevalence was −13.6 percentage points, with no statistically significant group difference.
results.detail: The absolute difference is calculated from the reported percentages. Chronic pain was defined as a visual analogue scale score ≥40 mm during stair climbing. The abstract does not describe adjudication or exclusion of other causes.
results.quote: The prevalence of chronic pain at 12 months was 17.4% (95% confidence interval [CI], 10.2%-27.9%) without difference between the ketamine (12.5%), nefopam (13.7%), and placebo groups (26.1%).

results.finding: In male Sprague-Dawley rats after thoracotomy (sample size unreported), rib-retraction allodynia lasted at least 40 days.
results.detail: Intercostal axon loss was observed in allodynic rats. The experiment did not selectively manipulate that injury or report time to resolution by analgesic treatment group.
results.quote: Allodynia appeared by Day 10 in the rib-retraction model and lasted at least 40 days.

results.finding: In a thoracotomy experiment in three sheep, complete intercostal nerve conduction block persisted 30 minutes after conventional retractor removal.
results.detail: Electrophysiological follow-up ended 30 minutes after retractor removal. The experiment did not measure persistent pain.
results.quote: The conduction block persisted 30 minutes after retractor placement and a further 30 minutes after removal (measurements 4 and 5).

results.finding: In 31 amputees, intrathecal and/or dorsal root ganglion lidocaine rapidly and reversibly abolished phantom limb pain.
results.detail: Dilute lidocaine also suppressed symptoms at concentrations the authors describe as sufficient to suppress ganglion ectopia while preserving conduction of impulses generated farther down the nerve.
results.quote: In 31 amputees, the local anesthetic lidocaine was applied intrathecally and/or to the DRG surface (intraforaminal epidural block). This rapidly and reversibly extinguished PLP and also nonpainful phantom limb sensation (npPLS). Control injections were ineffective.

results.finding: In 14 patients with persistent pain after inguinal hernia repair, bupivacaine tender-point blockade reduced pain by a median of 63%.
results.detail: The trial measured short-term pain relief after blocking a fascial plane. The authors report that the specific peripheral nerve lesion remained unidentified.
results.quote: The median (95% CI) reduction in pain was 63% (44.1 to 73.6%) after bupivacaine compared with 36% (11.6 to 49.7%; P=0.003) after placebo.

results.finding: Among 90 women undergoing modified radical mastectomy, perioperative lidocaine lowered postoperative serum IL-6 versus saline (P < 0.001).

results.finding: Among 88 analyzed VATS patients, perioperative lidocaine lowered mean serum IL-6 by 2.77 pg/mL versus saline at 24 hours.
results.detail: The regimen used a 1 mg/kg IV bolus, a 1.5 mg/kg/h intraoperative infusion, and lidocaine in postoperative patient-controlled analgesia. The paper provides no measured lidocaine concentrations or prespecified lidocaine safety endpoint results.
results.quote: Additionally, this study observed that intravenous lidocaine significantly reduced the expression levels of TNF-α, IL-1, and IL-6 in patients with lung cancer undergoing VATS surgery at 24 and 48 h postoperatively.

results.finding: Pectoserratus versus erector spinae plane block in mixed breast surgery (99 randomized, 76 assessed): pooled three-month chronic pain risk ratio 0.66.
results.detail: The primary outcome was perioperative opioid use. Chronic pain was classified from follow-up responses about pain duration, with blinded outcome assessors.
results.quote: Based on responses regarding the duration of pain, 22 of 42 patients (52%) in the PSPB group and 27 of 34 patients (79%) in the ESP block group were classified as experiencing chronic pain at 3 months (RR = 0.66, 95% CI 0.47 to 0.92, p = 0.02).

definition = "A treatment given around the time of a specified operation would reduce the risk of persistent pain by changing a biological process that causes it. Chronic postsurgical pain begins or worsens after surgery and persists beyond expected healing for at least three months after the operation. It is felt in the operated area, in the territory of a nerve there, or in an area to which pain from the operated tissues is referred. Diagnosis requires excluding other causes, including infection, malignancy and continuation of pre-existing pain.". Reason: The current definition omits the anatomical and diagnostic requirements and leaves unclear that the three months are counted from surgery.

goal.need = "About 1 in 10 surgical patients develops persistent pain and about 1 in 100 develops severe persistent pain. Greater pain severity is associated with more difficulty in daily activities six and twelve months later. Better pain relief in hospital can leave that risk intact. After major surgery, adding gabapentin slightly reduced pain on the first day, yet more patients reported pain four months later. Preventing the transition could spare patients months of pain and disability if the treatment addresses a cause of persistent pain for their operation.". Reason: The current paragraph gives prevalence figures but omits the effect on daily life and the clinical difference between early pain relief and prevention.

add statement by National Institute of Academic Anaesthesia and James Lind Alliance Research Priority Setting Partnership, 2015: "What can we do to stop patients developing chronic pain after surgery?". Reason: The partnership identifies prevention after surgery as a priority shared by patients, carers and clinicians.

add statement by European Medicines Agency, Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use, 2016: "prevent primarily acute pain after surgery or trauma developing into maladaptive chronic pain is a valid therapeutic target". Reason: The European medicines regulator explicitly recognizes prevention of the transition after surgery as a therapeutic target for drug development.

edit completion: title = "Independent trials replicate mechanism-based prevention of chronic postsurgical pain at twelve months."; set_by = "Atlas. No external body defines this combined test of causal mechanism, twelve-month clinical benefit, safety and independent replication."; basis = "IMMPACT recommends assessing postsurgical pain at 3, 6 and 12 months when feasible. The Federal Pain Research Strategy working group calls for mechanistic prevention trials that assess functional recovery. The Atlas selects the twelve-month endpoint and requires independent randomized replication, human evidence that the target contributes causally to prevention, and protocol-defined functional, healing and safety outcomes."; refs = [2, 3, 4, 5]. Reason: The title implies continuous observation for twelve months, and the basis attributes the independent-replication requirement to IMMPACT more strongly than its recommendations support.
add case "Limb amputation". Reason: IMMPACT identifies amputation as a prevention-trial population, and the European medicines guideline specifically identifies phantom limb pain after amputation.
add case "Inguinal hernia repair". Reason: IMMPACT identifies inguinal hernia repair as a distinct prevention-trial population with procedure-specific causes of persistent pain.
add case "Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery". Reason: The regional-anaesthesia analysis reports video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery separately from open thoracotomy.

add milestone after None: "Changing a biological target alters the duration of hypersensitivity in a surgical animal model.". Reason: A controlled intervention in one surgical model can establish a target's role in pain resolution before the broader validation required by m1.

edit m1: criterion = "Validate a target relevant to postsurgical pain in multiple animal models, by reproducing the finding in another laboratory, or by experimental validation in human tissue."; threshold_quote = "rigorously validating the target using multiple animal models, reproducing the work in another laboratory, or in human tissue etc."; threshold_ref = 6; refs = [6]. Reason: The single-model mouse result embedded in m1 tests an earlier stage and obscures the three alternative routes to validation.

edit m2: criterion = "In a controlled study of surgical patients, a perioperative dose that meets the protocol's safety criteria produces the intended change in an objective measure of the proposed biological target."; refs = [2]. Reason: The ketamine pilot's follow-up and pain risk ratio do not measure whether ketamine engaged its proposed target.

edit m3: title = "A randomized trial shows lower chronic postsurgical pain incidence at three months."; criterion = "A randomized superiority trial finds a lower incidence of adjudicated chronic postsurgical pain at three months with the perioperative intervention than with control. The confidence interval corresponding to the prespecified test lies wholly on the side of benefit: below 1 for an intervention-to-control risk ratio or below 0 for an intervention-minus-control risk difference. For an individual operation, apply the test to an estimate for that operation. ROCKet specifies a 95.1% interval for its pooled ketamine comparison."; set_by = "Committee for Proprietary Medicinal Products, guidance on superiority trials. IMMPACT recommends three-month assessment when feasible. Each protocol specifies its analysis and confidence level."; set_by_kind = "regulator"; threshold_quote = "it is the position of the confidence interval for the test statistic relative to this \u2018no difference\u2019 value that is of interest."; threshold_ref = 23; refs = [23, 3, 4, 5]. Reason: The 95.1% interval accounts for ROCKet's planned interim analysis and cannot serve as the confidence level for every intervention or operation.

edit m4: title = "One mechanistic trial reduces chronic postsurgical pain and pain-related disability at twelve months."; criterion = "In one randomized trial in a specified surgical population, the intervention achieves the prespecified reductions in chronic postsurgical pain and pain-related disability at twelve months. The trial verifies target engagement, demonstrates that changing the target contributes causally to prevention, and meets the protocol's healing and safety criteria."; refs = [2, 3, 5]. Reason: The pooled regional-anaesthesia estimates embedded in m4 do not establish a twelve-month effect on both pain and disability in a single mechanistic trial.
